# Synthetic tractography fixture

`synthetic.json` is authored for this package. It contains no patient data,
upstream track geometry, algorithms or measurements. Code values and attribute
VRs are public DICOM facts; the stored coordinates, colors, indices, measurements
and statistics are independently chosen. It is not generated by `Write`.

The test wire builder uses literal tags, VRs and standard-library byte packing,
without the production factory, restricted stream codecs or tag variables.
The JSON includes golden little-endian OF, OL and OW bytes. It has two sets,
three unequal-length tracks, nine points, every color level, two measurement
forms, both statistic families and an FD value that is not representable as FL.
Source references include Enhanced MR frames in the current study and selected
segmentation segments in another study.

Tests read the independently built object, validate its IOD and encoding, and
round-trip through Explicit VR LE and Implicit VR LE. Big-endian input and IEEE
special values have separate tests. The external DCMTK test runs only when an
explicit oracle executable path is supplied; it does not discover, download or
build tools. Passing synthetic tests is not proof of clinical interoperability.

The pinned DCMTK oracle preserves all modeled track-set families but has four
observed API/round-trip limits. It uses public measurement Values accessors and
restores SeriesNumber via a public setter. The whole-instance reference variant
matches all modeled families bidirectionally. Common metadata is not equivalent:
the reference also drops authored empty Laterality. No integral IOD round trip
is claimed. The complete [1,3] segment-selector case is asserted
non-equivalent because the reference drops those selectors; its original RED
observations are retained externally. This distinction does not relax the
mandatory complete fixture or the library's selector-preserving round trips.

The authored common metadata explicitly includes empty Laterality (0020,0060),
as a Type 2C value with unknown series-level side. No R/L value is inferred from
the two track sets. The writer preserves supplied metadata and does not insert
Laterality automatically. The initial dciodvfy missing-Laterality observation
remains in external evidence; the final authored inputs are separately qualified.
